newsitem.title: POLAND: Buba's Kuehbacher sees room to cut budget gap.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Kuehbacher sees room to cut budget gap.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher said on Wednesday that on current performance Germany's budget deficit this year could be 3.2-3.3 percent of GDP, but the government still had room to reduce it.
"My opinion is that if the current situation is prolonged to the end of December, the deficit could be about 3.2 to 3.3 percent," he told reporters after addressing a banking conference in Warsaw.
He added there was still room for manoeuvre to lower the deficit, for instance by raising taxes or reducing social transfers.
"The government and parliament can do something," he said, but he declined to speculate on the final outcome and said this depended on the extent of GDP growth and on the measures applied.
Kuehbacher said an offical working group now meeting in Schwerin was likely on Thursday to assess the shortfall in tax revenue for the year at 20 billion German marks.
"I think the results of (the meeting) will be that taxes in the central, state and local budgets will show tax revenues 20 billion deutschemarks lower than planned," he said.
"In line with social trends such as unemployment, we may have to spend five to eight billion deutschemarks extra, if you keep social transfers at the same level as last month," he added.
The shortfall figure of 20 billion marks has been widely cited by opposition and private sector officials, largely because of high unemployment.

The German government is considering freezing spending and raising borrowing levels for 1997 in order to plug holes in the budget deficit, Wolfgang Gerhardt, chairman of the centrist Free Democrats (FDP) said in Germany on Wednesday.
German Finance Minister Theo Waigel has refused to exclude a spending freeze as a possible remedy, and said the government would decide appropriate measures based on the tax estimate.
